出現在電影、影集、遊戲與廣告的配樂製作。音樂的長度與段落由畫面決定，一段可能只有: It appears in the scoring for film, series, games and advertising. The length and the sections of the music are decided by picture: a passage may last only a dozen seconds or run for several minutes. Recording usually goes session by session: first the passages that need the largest line-up, then solos and small sections, and last the pickups and fixes. The repertoire is not independent works but functional passages that go with the image, so one band in one day may record from the barest solo to a full-ensemble climax.
分譜準備、修改與現場重寫，速度決定成敗: Preparing and revising parts and rewriting on the spot; speed decides whether the session works
各類管樂，常兼奏加倍聲部: All kinds of wind, often doubling extra parts
同一段音樂可以用完整弦樂群錄，也可以用較少的樂手加上加倍錄音（overdub）疊: The same passage can be recorded with a full string body, or with fewer players stacked up through overdubs. Strings are the section most easily treated this way: record a small group, layer it a few times, and it sounds like a larger body. Winds and percussion are harder to do this with, because every added layer makes the sound thicker rather than wider. So the size of the line-up is often not a matter of what the music needs to sound like but a function of budget and time.
和劇場樂池相比，差別在時間的來源與可否重來。兩者都跟著畫面或舞台走，但樂池是一氣: Compared with the theatre pit, the difference is where the time comes from and whether you can do it again. Both follow the picture or the stage, but the pit is a live performance that runs straight through, and the music has to wait for the actual speed of the singers and actors; the scoring stage can record in sections, start again and patch afterwards, and the length of the music is, by contrast, fixed by picture that has already been cut.
在隔離錄音下重建一個不存在的合奏空間: Rebuilds, under isolated recording, an ensemble space that never existed
場次安排也反映音樂的結構。需要同一組樂手一起演奏的段落會被集中錄，獨奏與特殊樂器: The session plan reflects the structure of the music as well. Passages that need the same group of players together are recorded in one block, while solos and unusual instruments are scheduled separately. This division puts every hour in the stage where the most people are needed, and makes fixes easy: if only one solo line has to change, the whole band need not be called back. It is a way of breaking the music into units that can be handled separately, the exact opposite of a concert's logic of running straight through.
它的空間大小、隔間方式、麥克風位置、殘響設定，都直接決定聽到的聲音。同一個樂團在: Its size, the way it is divided into rooms, where the microphones stand and the reverb settings all directly decide what you hear. The same band, on the same day, in another stage with another set of microphones, can sound like two different bands. That is also why the "sound" of this line-up is hard to discuss apart from the recording environment: what the audience hears is not the band's sound in a room but a space the recording engineer has rebuilt at the console.
對片指揮，跟隨預編節拍器並配合固定畫面時間: Conducts to picture, following a pre-programmed click track and keeping to the fixed timing of the image
小提琴為首的弦樂群: A string body led by the violins
影視配樂編制（Film Scoring Session Orchestra）—: Film Scoring Session Orchestra — an ad hoc orchestra recording for picture, getting the music down in the scoring stage through sight-reading speed, a click track and isolated recording. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
影視配樂編制（film scoring session orchestra）是為: The film scoring session orchestra is an ad hoc orchestra that records for picture. Its members are called in by session, and in the scoring stage they turn the music the picture needs into recorded tracks after very little rehearsal. It does not run on long familiarity but on a highly standardised way of working: fast sight-reading, synchronising to picture, isolated recording. This line-up exists because of how film production divides its work and how it budgets, not because of any musical tradition.
影視配樂編制｜合奏與編制百科: Film Scoring Session Orchestra | Ensembles and instrumentation
成員是臨時召集的自由樂手，排練時間極短，部分聲部以隔離空間錄音，平衡由控台決定。: Its members are freelancers called in for the session, rehearsal time is very short, some sections are recorded in isolation, and the balance is decided at the console. It borrows the orchestra's instruments and layout, but it runs on the logic of the recording industry.
所以配樂棚本身就是一件樂器。: So the scoring stage is itself an instrument.
找有現場樂團錄音的製作。合成取樣與真人樂團的差別，在中低頻的厚度與起音的連貫上最: Look for productions that used a live orchestra. The difference between sampled and real players shows most clearly in the thickness of the low middle and the coherence of the attacks.
提供剪輯點、時間碼與當場的修改指示: Supplies cut points, timecode and changes on the spot
提供點綴、節奏與特殊音色: Supplies colour, rhythm and special timbres
最常被混為一談的是管弦樂團。樂器與座位幾乎相同，差別在時間由誰決定、聲音在哪裡形: The most common confusion is with the symphony orchestra. The instruments and seating are almost the same; the difference is who decides the time and where the sound is formed. An orchestra's tempo comes from the conductor and its balance is adjusted by ear in the hall on the spot; the film scoring session's tempo is locked by picture and click, some sections are recorded in isolation, and the balance is decided at the console after the take. The personnel are opposites too: one is a fixed organisation across seasons, the other freelancers called in by session.
注意弦樂的層次。加倍錄音的弦樂聽起來厚，但每一層的起音不完全一致，這種「不整齊的: Notice the layers in the strings. Overdubbed strings sound thick, but the attacks of each layer do not quite line up, and that uneven thickness is a signature of this line-up.
注意速度的穩定。對片錄音的速度由節拍器鎖定，聽起來會比音樂會版本更「方」，這是功: Notice how steady the tempo is. With the click locking the recording to picture, it sounds squarer than a concert version; that is a functional requirement, not a problem in the playing.
為什麼是這種編制而不是別的：: Why this line-up and not another:
獨奏線條與和聲厚度，依預算決定人數: Solo lines and harmonic weight; numbers decided by budget
當預算只夠小型編制，作曲家會把原本寫給完整管弦樂的聲部重新分配：讓木管兼奏原本的: When the budget covers only a small line-up, the composer redistributes parts written for a full orchestra: woodwinds double lines that would have been strings, or a synthesiser fills in the bass and percussion. This kind of reduction is not deleting a few parts from the score but deciding again which line can be sacrificed. The "orchestra" a listener hears on a soundtrack is sometimes a mid-sized band plus several layers of synth, not a full symphony orchestra.
節拍器與對片同步是第二道。: The click track and synchronising to picture are the second.
精準的是時間與音準，因為有節拍器與多次錄音；但現場的呼吸、動態與樂手之間的即時反: What is precise is time and intonation, thanks to the click and repeated takes; but the breathing, the dynamics and the instant reactions between players are weakened by isolated recording. The two trade different things.
編制的規模由預算與音樂風格決定，從十餘人的小型合奏到接近完整交響樂團的規模都有。: The size of the line-up is decided by budget and musical style, from small ensembles of a dozen or so players to something close to a full symphony orchestra. The players are freelance professionals; the same person may go in and out of several different scoring stages in one week. Besides the instrumental sections, the division of work adds several roles that do not exist at a concert.
編制縮放也牽動寫法。: Scaling the line-up changes the writing too.
聽空間感。同一張原聲帶裡，不同段落的殘響可能不一樣，因為它們是在不同棚、不同設定: Listen for the sense of space. On one soundtrack the reverb can differ from passage to passage, because they were recorded in different stages with different settings.
聽音樂與畫面的接點。注意音樂什麼時候進、什麼時候停，這些點通常對應剪輯，而不是樂: Listen for the joins between music and picture. Notice when the music enters and when it stops; those points usually match a cut, not a phrase.
與音樂會現場錄音的製作相比，差別在「一起呼吸」的有無。現場錄音保留樂手之間的即時: Compared with a live concert recording, the difference is whether the players breathe together. A live recording keeps the instant reactions between players and the reverb of the room; isolated scoring makes the separated sections independently controllable, at the cost of some of the physical reference, so the players have to rely more on the click and the monitors.
規模隨預算縮放。: The scale of the line-up scales with the budget.
讀譜速度是第一道門檻。: Sight-reading speed is the first hurdle.
這個編制的核心是: At the heart of this line-up is—
配樂棚裡，部分聲部或獨奏樂器（如銅管、打擊、人聲、電子樂器）會被隔離到獨立空間，: In a scoring stage some sections or solo instruments — brass, percussion, voices, electronic instruments — are put in separate rooms, hearing each other through headphones and mixed at the console; large orchestral sessions still play together in one room, using baffles only to help control bleed. This is nothing like a concert hall: in a hall the players hear each other's physical sound, and the balance is adjusted by ear on the spot; under isolated recording everyone hears sound that has been through microphones and a mix, and the balance is decided at the console after the take. The gain is that one section can be fixed on its own and the proportions adjusted later; the price is that the players lose the physical reference of breathing together and have to rely more on the click and the conductor.
配樂樂團就是一個交響樂團，只是演奏電影音樂。: A film scoring orchestra is just a symphony orchestra, only playing film music.
配樂的重點是旋律好聽。: What matters in film scoring is a good melody.
配樂總譜常在錄音當天才定稿，甚至現場還在改。樂手拿到的是第一次看到的譜，必須當場: The score is often finalised on the day of the recording, sometimes still being changed in the room. The players get music they are seeing for the first time and must judge on the spot where the parts are going, find their own place, and deal with modulations and changing metres. This does not come from memorising but from sight-reading built up over years: see a figure and you can predict what follows; see a marking and you know which kind of playing the composer wants. Being able to work under these conditions is the main filter in this world.
配樂首先要對準畫面：長度、剪輯點、情緒轉折都被影像鎖定。旋律只是達成這些功能的手: Film scoring first has to line up with picture: length, cut points and emotional turns are all fixed by the image. Melody is only one of the means to those ends, and many passages have no clear melody at all.
鋼琴、豎琴、打擊、有時含吉他與貝斯: Piano, harp, percussion, sometimes guitar and bass
錄音室版本一定比現場演出精準。: A studio version is always more precise than a live performance.
錄音時耳機裡有節拍器，畫面同步播放，譜上標著時間碼與剪輯點。節拍器讓速度精確到可: In the recording the headphones carry a click, the picture plays in sync, and the score is marked with timecode and cut points. The click keeps the tempo precise enough to match the length of the picture, and lets takes from different sessions be stacked together. Playing to picture means the rise and fall of the music has to follow the image: a pause has to land on a particular frame count, an accent has to hit the cut. The conductor's job is therefore not interpretation but coordination — watching the picture, giving the beat and checking that the band keeps up with the click, all at once. Tempo can be written in the score, but the rhythm of the picture will not wait.
隔離錄音改變了整個平衡邏輯。: Isolated recording changes the whole logic of balance.
音樂必須對準已經剪好的畫面，而畫面的長度不能改。因此時間不是由音樂決定，而是由影: The music has to line up with picture that has already been cut, and the length of the picture cannot change. So time is decided by the image, not by the music; and the band's make-up therefore tends towards professional players who can play a complex score correctly within a limited time, rather than towards a particular blend of timbres.
音準與弓法的基準，也是最大聲部: The reference for intonation and bowing, and the largest section
：錄音棚按小時計費，樂手按場次計酬，一首曲子通常只排一兩次就正式錄。所有設計都繞: : the scoring stage bills by the hour, the players are paid by the session, and a piece is usually rehearsed only once or twice before the take. Everything is designed around getting the first performance recorded well.
